key_facts.fact_en: Lump-sum construction contract dated 12 Jan 2026 for a villa in Al Awir First, AED 1,480,000, 8 months from site handover on 2 Feb 2026, supervised by Al Mirsam Engineering Consultants
The contract was signed before 1 June 2026, so the 1985 Civil Transactions Law still governs it; the claim relies on Article 4(1) of the new law, which does not apply to earlier acts
Variation order no. 1 (carport shade and extra paving), AED 46,500, approved on 14 Apr 2026 with the owner's consent, brings the work to AED 1,526,500
Final account: AED 1,526,500 of work, less 10% retention (AED 152,650) and AED 1,206,000 already paid under certificates 1 to 7, leaves AED 167,850 as the final payment

The printed retention (125,650) on the payment certificate is struck through and corrected by hand to 152,650, with the initials 'ك.ح' (the supervising engineer); only the corrected figure makes the table add up

The completion certificate records a joint inspection on 17 Sep 2026: the works are complete and fit for use except minor snags; the actual completion date, 14 Sep 2026, is written by hand only and starts the 12-month maintenance period
Handwritten snag list: a small water leak under the guest bathroom basin, repainting parts of the boundary wall, and fitting the kitchen cabinet handles, to be done within 14 days
The handwritten completion date (14 Sep 2026) falls inside the 8-month contract period that began on 2 Feb 2026, so no delay is apparent
The contractor gave the maintenance bank guarantee on 22 Sep 2026; the owner took over the villa on 5 Oct 2026 but has not paid despite a formal notice on 12 Oct 2026

reader_should_flag: Governing law: Federal Law No. 5 of 1985 (the old Civil Transactions Law) was repealed by Federal Decree-Law No. 25 of 2025 from 1 June 2026, but it still governs this contract, which was signed on 12 Jan 2026, before that date. The muqawala citations to the 1985 law (Arts. 872 to 874, 885 and 887(2)) are therefore the right ones (the new law's muqawala articles are 812 to 839).

The actual completion date (14 Sep 2026) is written by hand only, on the completion certificate (page 2), and is printed nowhere in the file. It starts the 12-month maintenance period, so it should be checked against the original certificate.

The retention on the final payment certificate (page 3) was corrected by hand: the printed 125,650 is struck through and replaced by 152,650, initialled 'ك.ح'. The corrected figure is 10% of the AED 1,526,500 work value, is the only one that makes the table add up (1,526,500 - 152,650 = 1,373,850), and is the figure the claim uses.
The snag list on the completion certificate is handwritten only (three items, to be completed within 14 days, i.e. by 5 Oct 2026).

Both sums were overdue when the claim was filed on 26 Oct 2026: the final payment from 8 Oct 2026 (14 days after the 24 Sep payment certificate) and the retention from 21 Oct 2026 (30 days after the 21 Sep completion certificate).
The hearing date (18 Nov 2026) appears only as a handwritten note on page 1.
